blocks.en: Abstract
blocks.zh: 摘要

blocks.en:
We introduce MultiFly, a real-world, low-altitude UAV dataset for semantic perception across RGB, thermal, LiDAR, and radar modalities.
MultiFly provides 17,272 synchronized samples from four suburban scenes with frame-wise annotations for 15 semantic classes, together with calibration and GNSS-RTK/IMU measurements.
To avoid costly and inconsistent modality-specific annotation, we propagate labels from only 115 manually annotated RGB images through shared geometric representations to all four modalities.
This approach generates semantic labels for 17,157 additional RGB images, 17,272 thermal images, 840M LiDAR points, and 3.4M radar points.
Transferred annotations achieve 89.93% average agreement with held-out manual annotations, and 90.94% average semantic consistency across all six modality pairs.
We further establish semantic segmentation benchmarks for all four modalities, revealing distinct architectural behavior for dense LiDAR and sparse radar data.
Taken together, MultiFly provides a scalable foundation for multimodal aerial perception and, to the best of our knowledge, the first public real-world low-altitude aerial benchmark that combines consistent frame-wise semantic annotations for RGB, thermal, LiDAR, and radar.
Data at https://github.com/markus-42/multifly .

blocks.en: I Introduction
blocks.zh: 一. 导言

blocks.en: Semantic scene understanding is fundamental to aerial perception [ 7 , 8 , 9 ] . However, unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) data remains substantially underrepresented in large-scale multimodal datasets, which increasingly drive modern foundation models. Notably, this is not simply a data-volume problem: UAV perception introduces distinct scene statistics, object scales, and viewing geometries, ranging from nadir to oblique perspectives, that are poorly represented in conventional ground-based datasets. Autonomous driving illustrates the contrast, where large-scale multimodal datasets have enabled systematic alignment across sensors, while similarly comprehensive resources for UAV perception remain limited.
blocks.zh: 语义场景理解对于空中感知[7,8,9]至关重要. 然而,无人驾驶飞行器(无人驾驶飞行器)的数据在大型多式数据集中仍然严重不足,这些数据集日益推动现代的基础模型。 值得注意的是,这不仅仅是一个数据量问题: 无人驾驶飞行器感知引入了不同的场景统计,对象尺度,并查看了从正角到斜角等不同角度的地貌,这些视角在传统的地基数据集中表现不佳. 自主驾驶说明了这种反差,即大型多式数据集能够使传感器之间系统一致,而用于无人驾驶飞行器感知的类似全面资源仍然有限。

blocks.en: This gap is particularly evident for semantic segmentation. Existing aerial datasets generally provide a single modality or limited modality combinations [ 10 , 5 , 6 ] , while no public real-world UAV dataset, to the best of our knowledge, provides synchronized frame-wise semantic annotations across RGB, thermal, LiDAR, and radar. Moreover, these modalities differ substantially in geometry and sampling, making consistent annotation difficult and costly.

blocks.en:
To address these challenges, we introduce MultiFly, a calibrated and time-synchronized four-modal aerial sensing platform and semantic dataset.
Our annotation framework uses 3D scene geometry as a common semantic interface: a sparse set of manually annotated RGB images is lifted into 3D and transferred to synchronized RGB, thermal, LiDAR, and radar measurements.
This yields dense multimodal annotations from only 115 manually labeled RGB images, while maintaining a common taxonomy and geometric reference.

这只从115个手动标注的RGB图像中产生密集的多式说明,同时保持一个通用的分类和几何参照.

blocks.en: II Related Work
blocks.zh: 二. 相关工作

blocks.en: II-A Multimodal Semantic Aerial Datasets
blocks.zh: II-A 多式联运语义航空数据集

blocks.en: Semantic perception has evolved from single-sensor benchmarks [ 11 , 12 ] toward multimodal datasets that enable learning across complementary sensors. In autonomous driving, early resources established core camera-LiDAR perception tasks, while second-generation datasets such as nuScenes [ 13 ] expanded to large-scale, synchronized multimodal sensing. This shift enabled not only sensor fusion, but also temporal and multi-task perception, prediction, and planning, and increasingly multimodal foundation models that unify these capabilities.
blocks.zh: 语义感知已经从单传感器基准[11,12]演变为能够跨越互补传感器学习的多式数据集. 在自主驱动中,早期资源建立了核心相机-LiDAR感知任务,而nuScens等第二代数据集则被扩展为大规模同步多模式感知. 这种转变不仅促成了传感器聚变,而且还促成了时间感知和多任务感知、预测和规划,以及使这些能力统一起来的日益多模式基础模型。

blocks.en:
UAV perception has yet to undergo a comparable transition. Existing aerial datasets remain fragmented across sensing modalities and annotation formats: most are unimodal [ 14 , 15 , 10 ] , while others combine only two modalities [ 3 , 16 , 6 ] , rely on synthetic data [ 17 , 18 ] , or provide map-wise rather than frame-wise annotations [ 19 , 20 ] . Consequently, the data required to develop and systematically evaluate unified multimodal UAV perception models remains largely unavailable. In particular, no public real-world low-altitude UAV dataset, to the best of our knowledge, provides synchronized frame-wise semantics across RGB, thermal, LiDAR, and radar.
MultiFly provides this missing substrate (Table I ), combining synchronized and registered RGB, thermal, LiDAR, and radar data with inertial measurements from Inertial Measurement Units (IMUs) and global positioning from a Global Navigation Satellite System (GNSS) with real-time kinematic (RTK) corrections.
blocks.zh:
无人驾驶航空器的感知尚未经历类似的转变。 现有的航空数据集在各种遥感方式和注释格式上仍然支离破碎:大多数是单式[14、15、10],而其他的只是将两种模式[3、16、6]结合起来,依靠合成数据[17、18],或者提供地图而不是框架说明[19、20]。 因此,开发并系统评价统一的多式无人驾驶飞行器感知模型所需的数据基本上仍未获得。 特别是,据我们所知,没有公共现实世界低空无人驾驶飞行器数据集提供跨RGB、热能、LiDAR和雷达的同步帧语义。
MultiFly提供了这一缺失的底物(表一),将同步和已注册的RGB、热能、LiDAR和雷达数据与惯性测量单元的惯性测量和全球导航卫星系统的全球定位结合,并进行实时动能(RTK)校正。

blocks.en: II-B Cross-Modal Semantic Consistency
blocks.zh: II-B 跨相模语义一致性

blocks.en:
Beyond sensor coverage, multimodal learning requires semantic supervision that is consistent across modalities. Independent annotation can introduce conflicting boundaries and labels, motivating geometry-based approaches that propagate semantics through a shared representation. KITTI-360 [ 21 ] transfers labels between images and 3D geometry, while WildScenes [ 22 ] projects multi-view image annotations into LiDAR.
UAVScenes [ 6 ] similarly annotates reconstructed 3D maps and renders them into camera frames before projecting labels onto LiDAR, while SegFly [ 5 ] adopts a 2D-3D-2D pipeline to lift sparse RGB annotations into a reconstructed point cloud and renders them into RGB and thermal images. These approaches demonstrate the feasibility of geometry-driven annotation, but remain limited in modality coverage, and require manual verification and correction.
blocks.zh:
除了传感器覆盖范围之外,多模式学习还需要各模式一致的语义监督。 独立的注释可以引入相冲突的边界和标签,激发以几何学为基础的方法,通过共同的表述来传播语义. KITTI-360 [21]在图像和3D几何之间转移标签,而WildScens [22] 将多视图图像说明投放到LiDAR.
UAVScens [6] 类似地注释重构了3D地图,并在将标签投放到LiDAR之前将其制成相机帧;而SegFly [5] 则采用2D-3D-2D管道将稀有的RGB注释提升到重建的点云中并被制作成RGB和热成像. 这些方法表明,几何学驱动的注释是可行的,但模式覆盖范围仍然有限,需要人工核实和纠正。

blocks.en: MultiFly extends this paradigm to four modalities through a unified geometry-driven pipeline, propagating sparse RGB annotations to RGB, thermal, LiDAR, and radar, while ensuring high semantic consistency without the necessity of manual correction. It therefore offers not only broader sensor coverage, but a shared frame-wise semantic reference for multimodal UAV perception and cross-modal evaluation.
blocks.zh: MultiFly通过统一的几何驱动管将这一范式扩展到了四种模式,向RGB,热能,LiDAR和雷达传播了稀疏的RGB注释,同时确保高语义一致性而无需人工校正. 因此,它不仅提供了更广泛的传感器覆盖范围,而且为多式联运无人驾驶航空器感知和跨模式评价提供了共同的帧语义参考。

blocks.en: III-A Design
blocks.zh: 三-A 设计

blocks.en:
To acquire multimodal aerial data, we propose the MultiFly platform shown in Fig. 2 , which integrates one forward-facing RGB camera, one thermal camera, one spinning LiDAR, two forward-facing radars, and a GNSS-RTK-aided inertial navigation system (INS), with detailed specifications listed in Table II .
One radar is pitched downward by 14 ∘ 14^{\circ} to increase the effective vertical field of view (FOV), while the whole sensor rig is pitched downward by 45 ∘ 45^{\circ} to jointly observe the flight direction and ground below the UAV.
All perception sensors are calibrated with respect to the LiDAR reference frame and synchronized to a common time base, while the INS provides the platform pose.
Perception data are recorded at 10 ​ Hz 10\,\mathrm{Hz} on an Aetina AIB MX22 edge computing unit using Docker and ROS 2 Humble, together with dedicated onboard power (DOGCOM 10000 mAh Li-Ion), networking (NetGear GSM110MX switch), and storage hardware.
Example synchronized RGB, thermal, LiDAR, and radar measurements are shown in Fig. 4 .

blocks.en: III-B Time Synchronization
blocks.zh: 三-B 时间同步

blocks.en:
All sensors are synchronized to a common GNSS-disciplined time base using the Precision Time Protocol (PTP).
The INS acts as the PTP grandmaster, while the Aetina computer operates as a boundary clock and distributes the time reference to the sensor network.
While PTP establishes a common time base, sensor-specific triggering and phase compensation align the actual acquisition times across modalities.
More specifically, sensor acquisition is aligned with the LiDAR’s 10 Hz 10\text{\,}\mathrm{Hz} scan cycle, corresponding to a fixed rotation period of 100 ms 100\text{\,}\mathrm{ms} .
The rotating LiDAR generates a hardware trigger for the forward-facing RGB camera, with a configurable delay accounting for the exposure time and the camera’s orientation relative to the LiDAR scan, effectively aligning the acquisition with the LiDAR beam passing through the camera FOV.
The radars operate at the same nominal frequency, but their measurement epochs have a deterministic phase offset relative to the LiDAR cycle, which
is compensated using the driver’s cycle_offset parameter, resulting in radar–LiDAR deviations within ± 3 ms \pm 3\text{\,}\mathrm{ms} .
Since the thermal camera does not support hardware triggering, its acquisition is controlled using timestamped GigE Vision Scheduled Action Commands, which are executed according to its PTP-synchronized clock.

blocks.en: Radar detections are transformed into the LiDAR frame, and LiDAR-frame measurements are projected into either image using the calibrated extrinsics, intrinsics, and distortion models.

blocks.en:
Furthermore, RGB–thermal registration requires scene geometry because the nonzero camera baseline induces depth-dependent parallax. Consequently, the calibrated rigid extrinsic alone does not define a dense pixel-to-pixel mapping.
In principle, the synchronized and calibrated LiDAR measurements could provide the required depth for reprojecting RGB observations into the thermal view.
Instead, we follow SegFly [ 5 ] and use the metric RGB-based 3D reconstruction required by the label-transfer pipeline ( Section IV-A ).
This reconstruction already provides scene-wide geometry and
RGB image–point correspondences.
Naturally, using the same geometric representation for both registration and semantic label transfer ensures consistency between both stages.
Our choice therefore does not reflect a limitation of LiDAR, but avoids
introducing a separate geometric representation for registration. Moreover, unlike SegFly [ 5 ] , whose acquisition setting requires an independent thermal reconstruction and iterative closest point (ICP) alignment, our cameras are synchronized and rigidly calibrated.
We therefore retain the fixed RGB–thermal extrinsic and require neither thermal reconstruction nor ICP.

blocks.en:
Technically, for each synchronized RGB–thermal pair, the thermal camera pose is obtained by composing the corresponding RGB reconstruction pose with the fixed RGB–thermal extrinsic.
Reconstructed landmarks jointly visible in both cameras are projected into their undistorted image planes using the calibrated camera models.
Because each pair of projections represents the same physical
3D point, it identifies where scene content visible to the thermal camera appears in the corresponding RGB frame.
Following SegFly, these projected landmarks determine the common image support used to warp the original RGB image.
In particular, the RGB image is resampled from its distorted image plane into a common undistorted pinhole domain and subsequently mapped into the thermal distortion space.
The valid overlap is cropped and resized to the thermal resolution, while pixels mapped outside the valid common support are masked.
This process yields a registered RGB image on the pixel grid of every thermal image.

blocks.en:
Our goal is to generate dense semantic annotations for all four sensor modalities from only a sparse set of manually annotated RGB source views. With these, we aim to produce the complete collections of time-synchronized, frame-wise semantic labels 𝒴 ^ RGB \widehat{\mathcal{Y}}^{\mathrm{RGB}} , 𝒴 ^ Th \widehat{\mathcal{Y}}^{\mathrm{Th}} , 𝒴 ^ Lid \widehat{\mathcal{Y}}^{\mathrm{Lid}} and 𝒴 ^ Rad \widehat{\mathcal{Y}}^{\mathrm{Rad}} for the RGB, thermal, LiDAR and radar modalities, respectively.
The following subsections describe how these four sets are obtained via geometry-driven label transfer.
While the individual transfer operations build on established geometry-driven methods [ 5 , 21 , 22 ] , our contribution is their modality-specific adaptation and integration into a unified aerial framework that derives consistent RGB, thermal, LiDAR, and radar labels from the same sparse set of manually annotated RGB views.

blocks.en: V-A Data Acquisition and Source Annotation

blocks.en:
We collect MultiFly using the EmQopter Q6500 UAV ( Fig. 1 ) together with the calibrated and time-synchronized platform described in Section III .
The acquisition campaign comprises four suburban scenes within the metropolitan area of Ingolstadt in Germany, recorded during summer under sunny and cloudy conditions.
Each scene is surveyed at nominal flight altitudes of 30 ​ m 30\,\mathrm{m} and 50 ​ m 50\,\mathrm{m} above ground level.
At each altitude, the UAV follows an automated double-grid trajectory, in line with the acquisition strategy of OccuFly [ 24 ] .
The flight speed is 3 ​ m ​ s − 1 3\,\mathrm{m}\,\mathrm{s}^{-1} and the flight lines are planned with a nominal RGB side overlap of 40 % 40\text{\,}\% .
During all flights the sensor stack is pitched downward by 45 ∘ 45^{\circ} relative to the horizontal to observe both the flight direction and the terrain below.
To reduce temporal redundancy while retaining meaningful scene variation, the synchronized 10 Hz perception streams are subsampled by selecting every second frame at 30 m 30\text{\,}\mathrm{m} and every third frame at 50 m 50\text{\,}\mathrm{m} .
The INS records at 100 Hz 100\text{\,}\mathrm{H}\mathrm{z} and its complete navigation stream is preserved at the original temporal resolution.
The LiDAR records a full 360 ∘ 360^{\circ} azimuth during acquisition.
During offline preprocessing, each LiDAR scan is restricted to the 90 ∘ 90^{\circ} sector facing forward and aligned with the RGB camera.

blocks.en:
Evaluation Protocol. We evaluate the semantic consistency of the final MultiFly labels across all modality pairs without relying on intermediate 3D representations or additional manual ground truth.
Results are summarized in Table V .
We distinguish three types of modality pairs:
blocks.zh:
评价协议。 我们评价所有模式配对中最终多Fly标签的语义一致性,而不依赖于中间的3D表示或额外的手动地面真理.
结果摘要见表五。
我们区分三种模式对:

blocks.en:
2D–2D (RGB–Thermal) :
We reuse the geometry-driven 2D–3D–2D registration ( Section III-D ), but apply it to the RGB semantic labels instead of the RGB image.
The labels are warped onto the thermal image grid via the recovered mapping, after which pixel-wise agreement with the thermal labels is measured.
blocks.zh:
2D–2D(RGB-热) :
我们重用由几何驱动的2D–3D–2D注册(第三节-D),但应用到RGB语义标签而不是RGB图像.
标签通过回收的映射被扭曲到热成像网格上,然后与热成像素协议进行测量.

blocks.en:
2D–3D (RGB/Thermal – LiDAR/Radar) :
For each synchronized frame, we project the LiDAR or radar points into the corresponding RGB or thermal image using the calibrated extrinsics, intrinsics.
The semantic label of each valid projected point is compared with the label of the projected pixel.
blocks.zh:
2D–3D (RGB/热能 – LiDAR/Radar) :
对于每个同步相框,我们利用被校正的外相,内在的将LiDAR或雷达点投射到相应的RGB或热成像.
每个有效投影点的语义标签被与投影像素的标签进行比较.

blocks.en:
3D–3D (LiDAR–Radar) :
Since radar returns are substantially sparser than LiDAR point clouds, we establish cross-modal correspondences using nearest-neighbor association. For each radar point, we identify the closest LiDAR point within a fixed Euclidean distance threshold r r and compare their semantic labels. We set r = 1 ​ m r=1\,\mathrm{m} , which provides a correspondence for 71 % 71\text{\,}\% of the radar points. Semantic agreement is then determined over these points.
We further evaluate the sensitivity to the choice of r r in the results.

For all modality pairs, only pixels/points that yield a valid semantic class (i.e., neither c unl c_{\mathrm{unl}} nor c inv c_{\mathrm{inv}} ) are considered.
We report consistency as the percentage of agreeing label pairs.

Results. As shown in Table V , MultiFly achieves an average cross-modal semantic consistency of 90.94 % 90.94\text{\,}\% across all six modality pairs and all four scenes.
For the LiDAR–Radar pair, the consistency remains robust to the choice of association radius, with r = { 0.1 , 0.25 , 0.5 , 1.0 , 2.0 } ​ m r=\{0.1,0.25,0.5,1.0,2.0\}\,\mathrm{m} yielding { 96 , 95 , 95 , 93 , 93 } % \{96,95,95,93,93\}\,\% agreement, respectively, while an unconstrained nearest-neighbor association ( r = ∞ r=\infty ) yields 86 % 86\,\% .
Since all evaluations rely on the calibrated intrinsics, extrinsics, and the RGB–thermal registration, the high agreement also serves as a proxy for geometric fidelity.

结果。 如表五所示,MultiFly在所有6个模式对和所有4个场景中平均实现90.94%90.94%的跨模式语义一致.
对于LiDAR-Radar一对,在选择关联半径上的一致性仍然很强,r = {0.1,0.25,0.5,1.0,2.0} m r r = 0.0.25,0.5,1.0,2.0 \}\,\mathrm{m} 生成 { 96,95,95,95,93}% 96,95,95,93 \}\, \%, \%,而一个不受约束的相邻关联(r = ∞ r r=\infty) 的产值为 86\ 86\,\%.
由于所有评价都依赖于校正的内在因素、外在因素和RGB-热量登记,因此,高分协议也充当了几何忠诚的代名词。

blocks.en:
Notably, this performance is achieved although our approach employs static 3D reconstruction for label propagation and point-cloud aggregation, which could affect dynamic objects.
While 4D reconstruction methods [ 25 ] are a promising direction for addressing this limitation in future work, our results confirm that our label transfer ensures both semantically consistent and geometrically coherent multimodal aerial data under this challenging setting.
blocks.zh:
值得注意的是,虽然我们的方法采用了静态的3D重建来进行标签传播和点-云集,这可能会影响动态物体,但还是实现了这种性能.
虽然4D重建方法[25]是未来工作中解决这一局限性的一个有希望的方向,但我们的结果证实,在这种具有挑战性的环境下,我们的标签转让既确保了整体一致性,又确保了多式航空数据的几何一致性。

blocks.en: VI-C Annotation Efficiency
blocks.zh: VI-C 说明效率

blocks.en:
Only 115 115 ( 0.67 % 0.67\% ) of MultiFly’s 17,272 17{,}272 RGB frames serve as manually annotated source views, taking 29 min 29\text{\,}\mathrm{m}\mathrm{i}\mathrm{n} on average per frame.
From this small subset, the geometry-driven pipeline automatically
labels the remaining 17,157 17,157 RGB frames, all 17,272 17,272 thermal frames, 8.4 × 10 8 8.4\times 10^{8} LiDAR points, and 3.4 × 10 6 3.4\times 10^{6} radar points.
No thermal frame or 3D point is manually annotated for data generation.
The resulting labels exhibit high semantic quality within each modality ( Table IV ), and strong semantic consistency across modalities ( Table V ).
Taken together, these results provide strong empirical evidence that sparse RGB annotations can be automatically propagated at scale to generate high-quality, semantically consistent 2D and 3D labels across four modalities without manual refinement.

blocks.en: VII-A Experimental Setup
blocks.zh: VII-A 实验设置

blocks.en:
We benchmark established semantic segmentation architectures to assess whether our dataset provides effective supervision for learning semantic representations from its annotated modalities.
The RGB and thermal benchmarks follow the cross-modal training protocol of SegFly [ 5 ] , including RGB-to-thermal adaptation using registered image pairs. LiDAR and radar models are trained independently for their respective modalities. The benchmark therefore evaluates both cross-modal image adaptation and modality-specific 3D segmentation, while dataset-level semantic consistency is assessed separately in Section VI-B .
blocks.zh:
我们以既定的语义分类结构为基准,评估我们的数据集是否有效监督从其附加说明的方式学习语义表述。
RGB和热能基准遵循了SegFly[5]的跨模式训练协议,包括使用已注册的图像对进行RGB到热能改造. LiDAR和雷达模型分别接受各自模式的独立培训. 因此,该基准既评价跨模式图像的适应性,也评价特定模式的三维分解,而数据集层面的语义一致性则在第六-B节中单独评估.

blocks.en:
Leveraging MultiFly’s four distinct scenes, we adopt a strict held-out-scene protocol to assess scene-level generalization, using scenes 1–3 exclusively for training and scene 4 exclusively for final evaluation.
All models are evaluated using their official configurations.
blocks.zh:
利用MultiFly的四大场景, 我们采用严格的预留场景协议来评估场景层面的概括,
所有模型都使用其官方配置进行评估.

blocks.en: VII-B RGB and Thermal Semantic Segmentation
blocks.zh: VII-B RGB和热语义分解

blocks.en:
We benchmark established UPerNet-Swin-S [ 26 ] , SegFormer-MiT-B3 [ 27 ] , and Firefly [ 5 ] for RGB and thermal semantic segmentation.
All methods use their official implementations and configurations, including pretrained encoders or backbones, but without external task-specific segmentation checkpoints.
Following SegFly [ 5 ] , training comprises three stages: RGB training, RGB-to-thermal adaptation using registered MultiFly RGB–thermal pairs, and thermal fine-tuning.
All models are trained for 30 epochs for RGB training, 10 epochs for RGB-to-thermal adaptation, and 30 epochs for thermal fine-tuning.
We report the final-epoch results.
blocks.zh:
我们建立了UPerNet-Swin-S [26],SegFormer-Mit-B3 [27],以及用于RGB和热语义分解的萤火虫[5]。
所有方法都使用其正式执行和配置,包括经过预先训练的编码器或骨干,但没有针对具体任务的外部分区检查站.
继SegFly[5]之后,培训包括三个阶段: RGB培训,使用已注册的多Fly RGB-热配对进行RGB-对热的适应,并进行热微调.
所有型号都经过了30个世纪的RGB训练,10个世纪的RGB对热适应,30个世纪的热微调.
我们报告最终结果。

blocks.en:
As shown in Table VI , Firefly achieves the strongest performance for both RGB and thermal semantic segmentation in terms of mean intersection over union (mIoU) and mean accuracy (mAcc).
Qualitative predictions for a representative sample in Fig. 6 are consistent with the quantitative results, demonstrating that MultiFly supports effective semantic segmentation across both modalities.
blocks.zh:
如表六所显示,萤火虫在RGB和热语义分解方面,在结合(mIoU)和平均精度(mAcc)上的平均相交点方面都取得了最强的性能.
图6中有代表性的样本的定性预测与定量结果一致,表明多氟支持两种模式的有效语义分化.

blocks.en: VII-C LiDAR and Radar Semantic Segmentation
blocks.zh: VII-C LiDAR和雷达语义分解

blocks.en:
We benchmark state-of-the-art SparseUNet (SpUNet) [ 28 ] , LitePointTransformer-S (LitePT) [ 29 ] , and PointTransformerV3 (PTv3) [ 30 ] independently on the LiDAR and radar labels.
All methods use their official implementations and configurations unless stated otherwise.
In addition to 3D coordinates, the LiDAR inputs include intensity, while the radar inputs include radar cross section (RCS) and Doppler velocity, in line with [ 14 ] .
Each model is trained separately for LiDAR and radar semantic segmentation for 20 epochs, and we report the final-epoch results.
For radar, the only configuration change is an increase in the voxelization grid-size from 0.05 m 0.05\text{\,}\mathrm{m} to 0.50 m 0.50\text{\,}\mathrm{m} , providing a coarser discretization
to account for the lower density of radar points.
blocks.zh:
我们把最先进的SparseUNet(Spunet)[28],LitePoint Transformer-S(LitePT)[29],以及LiDAR和雷达标签上独立的Point TransformerV3(PTv3)[30]作为基准.
除非另有说明,所有方法都使用其正式实施和配置。
除了3D坐标外,LiDAR输入还包括了强度,而雷达输入包括了雷达跨段(RCS)和多普勒速度,符合[14].
每个模型都分别用于LiDAR和雷达语义分解20个纪元,我们报告最终纪元结果.
对于雷达来说,唯一的配置变化是将voxelization网格的大小从0.05 m 0.05\text~,}\-mathrm{m}提高到了0.50 m 0.50\text~,}\-mathrm{m},提供了相近的光碟化.
以说明雷达点密度较低。

blocks.en:
As shown in Table VII , PTv3 performs best on LiDAR, whereas SpUNet achieves the strongest radar performance.
Prior work identifies sparse-convolutional approaches for sparser radar point clouds as an understudied area [ 14 ] .
By benchmarking SpUNet against recent point-transformer architectures, we directly address this gap and find that established sparse convolutions can outperform recent attention-based models.
This result provides a promising initial benchmark for radar semantic segmentation, while controlled studies are required to disentangle the effects of individual architectural choices.
Qualitative predictions for a representative sample in Fig. 7 further support the quantitative results.
blocks.zh:
如表七所示,PTv3在LiDAR上表现最好,而Spunet则能实现最强的雷达性能.
先前的工作将稀有地层的雷达点云的方法确定为研究不足的区域[14].
通过将Spunet与最近的点变结构作为基准,我们直接解决了这一差距,并发现既有的零星演变可以比最近基于关注的模型更好。
这一结果为雷达语义分解提供了一个有希望的初步基准,同时需要进行有控制的研究来分解单个建筑选择的影响.
图7中的代表性样本的质量预测进一步支持了定量结果.

blocks.en: VIII Conclusion
blocks.zh: 八 结论

blocks.en:
We introduce MultiFly, a real-world low-altitude UAV dataset with synchronized RGB, thermal, LiDAR, and radar semantic annotations.
By propagating labels from only 115 manually annotated RGB images, MultiFly provides dense supervision across 17,272 multimodal samples with high annotation agreement and cross-modal consistency.
Our benchmarks further establish initial semantic segmentation baselines for all four modalities.
blocks.zh:
我们引入了MultiFly,一个真实世界的低空无人驾驶飞行器数据集,并配有同步的RGB,热能,LiDAR和雷达语义说明.
通过仅从115个手动附加说明的RGB图像中宣传标签,MultiFly为17,272个多式联运样本提供了密集的监管,具有高注释协议和跨模式一致性.
我们的基准进一步确定了所有四种模式的初步语义分化基线。
